newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa to undergo second brain scan.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa to undergo second brain scan.

text.p: Mother Teresa will undergo a second brain scan this week before doctors consider releasing her from hospital where she is recovering from a fall, a physician treating the missionary said on Monday.
"The next course of her treatment will be decided after a repeat CAT (brain) scan on Wednesday," said Dr S.K. Sen, medical director of Woodlands Nursing Home hospital.

The 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun, who spent nearly three weeks at Woodlands in late August and early September for heart trouble, malaria and pneumonia, was again taken to the hospital on September 16 after falling from a chair.
The doctors later detected a black spot on her brain after conducting an initial scan. They said it could be a haemorrhage or stem from an earlier injury.
Last week, doctors said they expected the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner to undergo a second scan on Monday and possibly leave hospital the next day.
But doctors said now they wanted to wait longer so that the second scan would indicate whether the spot represented a fresh injury or was older.
The hospital gave an upbeat medical report. "Mother Teresa is doing well and remains cheerful," it said in a daily medical bulletin.
"She is much better now and there is no neurological complication," Sen said.
